**A clinical triage model must be evaluated as part of a human workflow.** The threshold determines how many cases are escalated and how many affected cases are missed. A default probability cutoff of 0.5 has no inherent clinical justification. Define intended use and consequences with qualified clinical experts. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.07511) [2](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/artificial-intelligence-enabled-medical-devices/transparency-machine-learning-enabled-medical-devices-guiding-principles)

Sensitivity at a manageable review burden may be more relevant than overall accuracy in a rare-condition setting. Probability calibration and threshold choice are separate: a calibrated model can still be used with an unsuitable threshold.

**Uncertainty sets can support deferral, but their guarantee has limits.** Standard split conformal coverage is marginal under exchangeability; it does not establish equal sensitivity at every hospital or for every subgroup. A large ambiguous set should trigger a defined next step rather than delay urgent assessment.

Evaluate external sites, time shifts, missing data, subgroup outcomes, and the combined human–AI process. Prospective validation and applicable oversight determine fitness for deployment. This is an architecture and evaluation answer, not a diagnostic recommendation; a technically correct confidence method cannot substitute for evidence that the workflow improves care.

**Technical details and references.**

Define the intended clinical workflow and false-negative cost with clinical experts; optimize sensitivity at an acceptable workload and false-positive burden, using representative validation data rather than a default 0.5 threshold. Calibrate probabilities separately from choosing thresholds. Conformal sets can trigger deferral when ambiguous, but standard split conformal provides **marginal** coverage under exchangeability, not 95% sensitivity for every hospital, demographic, or disease subgroup. Evaluate external hospitals, temporal shifts, missingness, subgroup calibration, and the human–AI team's performance. Design a clear escalation route and prevent automation from delaying urgent assessment. This is a system-design answer, not a diagnostic recommendation; prospective clinical validation and applicable oversight determine whether it is fit for use.
